extracted_information: This article details methods for detecting process injection, a form of memory injection, in Windows environments. It covers evasion techniques used by adversaries and corresponding detection strategies for memory-resident malware, focusing on the logging mechanisms and telemetry sources available to defenders.

features.name: Antivirus / Antimalware
features.description: Detects stage-less implants loaded from disk based on signatures. Can be augmented with Yara Rules.

features.name: Application Isolation and Sandboxing
features.description: Performs automated dynamic analysis of suspicious binaries in a sandbox before execution. Examples: Hybrid Analysis (CrowdStrike Falcon® Sandbox), Any Run.

features.name: Code Signing Enforcement
features.description: Restricts execution of unsigned or unknown applications. Example: Windows AppLocker.

features.name: Execution Prevention
features.description: Prevents unauthorized code execution. Example: Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC).

features.name: Kernel Callback Monitoring
features.description: EDRs use kernel-mode drivers to register callbacks for process creation, image loading, and handle operations to gain telemetry and inject hooking libraries. Examples: PsSetCreateProcessNotifyRoutine*, ObRegisterCallbacks(), PsSetLoadImageNotifyRoutine*, PsSetCreateThreadNotifyRoutine*.

features.name: API Hooking (Usermode)
features.description: Injecting hooking libraries to detour functions by overwriting function bodies (inline hooks) or modifying Import Address Tables (IAT hooks) to intercept API calls like memory allocation and write operations. Bypasses PatchGuard limitations.

features.name: Call Stack Analysis
features.description: Analyzes call stacks during syscall execution to detect anomalous direct syscalls (e.g., direct return to user code not through normal wrappers or custom syscall stubs) or artificially legitimized call stacks (ROP gadgets, hardware breakpoints). Utilizes Process Instrumentation Callback.

features.name: Event Tracing for Windows (ETW)
features.description: Leverages the Threat-Intelligence (TI) log provider to receive telemetry on memory allocation, modification, protection changes, and thread operations without relying on hooking. Detects Process Hollowing and ETW tampering.

features.name: Memory Type and Protection Analysis
features.description: Monitors for anomalous memory characteristics, such as private memory marked as executable (RWX), fluctuating memory protections (RW ⇄ RX), or unshared MEM_MAPPED/MEM_IMAGE pages (indicating memory patching or hooks).

features.name: Memory Scanning
features.description: Event-triggered scans of memory regions to detect PE headers ('MZ') in private memory (PE Injection) or unusually large buffer sizes in remote memory writes (indicating shellcode).

features.name: Process Doppelgänging/Phantom DLL Hollowing Detection
features.description: Identifies this technique by checking for `GetMappedFileNameW()` failures or using `MmDoesFileHaveUserWritableReferences()` to detect broken section coherency.

features.name: Thread Execution Monitoring
features.description: Detects suspicious thread creation (e.g., starting address pointing to private memory), thread context modification (`SetThreadContext()`), or Asynchronous Procedure Calls (APCs).

features.name: Message Hook Detection
features.description: Identifies suspicious message hook functions (`SetWindowsHookEx()`) often abused by keyloggers, through enumerating `gSharedInfo` members, API hooking, or stateful anomaly detection.

features.name: Pointer/Callback Overwrite Detection
features.description: Monitors for writes to executable memory regions or known callback pointers (e.g., PROPagate, ConsoleWindowClass, AddressOfEntryPoint, TLS callbacks, Ctrl-Inject, KernelCallbackTable PEB member) to detect redirection of execution flow.

features.name: Exploit Protection Mechanisms
features.description: Mitigations like Control Flow Guard (CFG) and Data Execution Prevention (DEP) are designed to limit exploitation of memory corruption vulnerabilities and prevent execution of non-code regions.
